Lauren Brochu - SDS 313 UT Austin

Introduction

The Grape Quality Dataset includes grape samples, each of which cover variables such as identification, geographic, quality metrics, physical metrics, and environmental factors. I picked this data set to anyalyze because I saw promise of meeting many of the choice elements, and I’ll be attempting to investigate how different grape quality metrics correlate with overall quality ratings.

https://www.presetpro.com/landscape-photography-napa-valley/

Data Preperation

In order to prepare this data, I uploaded all of the libraries I knew I would need. I converted all of the dates into month-day-year format, and then changed the Quality Category variable into a numeric value for simplified future analysis. After this, I made two variables: A Weather Impact Index, and a Sugar Acidity Ratio. This was accomplished using if statements within for loops. The biggest challenge I faced was making a new Harvest Date variable in month-day-year format because every time I would make a graph, it would reset to it’s original format. There were no NA values, and there were 1000 observations.

Variable Descriptions

Variable Summary
Variable Names Type Description
variety Character The type of grape variety grown.
region Character The geographical location where the grapes were grown.
clusterWeightG Numeric The weight of a grape cluster in grams.
berrySizeMM Numeric The size of individual grape berries measured in millimeters.
harvestDate Date The date when the grapes were harvested.
qualityRating Numeric Grape quality rating, ranked 1 for Premium, 2 for High, 3 for Medium, and 4 for Low.
weatherImpactIndex Numeric An index summarizing the impact of environmental conditions like rainfall, soil moisture, and sun exposure on grape quality.
sugarAcidRatio Numeric A ratio of sugar content to acidity, used to evaluate the sweetness-acidity balance of the grapes.
harvestDateFormatted Character New Harvest Date variable in month day year format.
harvestMonth Ordered Factor Month of which grape samples were harvested.

Univariate Analysis

The distribution of Grapes by Region is visually very uniform, suggesting minimal bias in the original dataset’s collection. Rioja had the least amount of grape recordings at 107, while 137 represents the most objects in Napa Valley.

While not as uniform as the region distribution, the frequency of grape variety still doesn’t suggest collection bias. However, the graph does not reflect acreage of vineyard grape production as might be assumed. Cabernet Sauvignon wine grapes have approximately 713,592 acres of dedicated land, and Merlot wine grapes have about 660,302 acres — yet neither of these are ranked highest in frequency within the sample (Puckette, 2011). Of the 1000 grape samples, 146 of them are from Pinot Noir grapes, and 113 are from Merlot grapes.

The grapes have a relatively large range in cluster weight at 299.67 grams. The median of the data is 195.285 grams.

The Weather Impact Index takes account of the number of hours each grape cluster spent in the sun, the moisture percentage, along with the rainfall in mm. Given this, the range of the boxplot is 9.1786. The median of the data is 7.7343, while the mean of the variable is 7.6844172. Because these values are so close in comparison to the range, it is still mainatined that there is no skew in the dataset.

Multivariate Analysis

Cabernet Sauvignon appears to have the most prominent presence among regions and remains relatively consistent throughout all of them. Nappa Valley and Sonoma have a good overall balance of grape samples, while Rioja, Bordeaux, and Loire Valley are more largely variable. In Napa Valley, Cabernet Sauvignon accounts for 15 entries, which is approximately 10.9489051% of the total Napa Valley grapes.

While the graph itself appears to have a poor correlation, represented by the value 0.2320405, the apparent gradient created by the color index shows a correlation. The most abundant number of “High” quality rating (see variable table) is clustered where the weather impact index and the sugar acid ratio is the highest. As both of these variables decrease, as does the quality rating.

The Average Weather Impact Index is calculated by grouping data from Harvest Month and Quality Rating, to then take the mean of the Weather Impact Index within each group. Given this, it’s apparent that lower quality ratings are associated with higher average Weather Impact Index, and vice versa. This could be because increased environmnetal conditions have higher impact on grape cluster quality. The standard deviation within the graph is 1.9170569 while the mean is 7.6844172. This suggests a low variability in environmental conditions within the dataset.

Reproducibility

In order to make this reproducible, I made sure to include links to everything, and outline regular comments to ensure code chunks make sense in addition to separating code blocks by each purpose. I also made sure to include all imported libraries at the beginning.

Choice Elements

The choice elements I used were [1] using 5 or more in-line codes, [2] making two new variables of interest, [3] formatting a date, [4] formatting a string, [5] and using an if statement to make two new variables. [1] Occurred 1 or more times under every single graph desription, mainly, but not limited to means / medians, ranges, and standard deviation. [2] Occurred in the making of a Weather Impact Index, and a Sugar to Acidity Ratio. [3] Occurred when changing the dates from Ymd into mdY. [4] Occurred when changing the Quality Category into a numeric value. [5] Occurred by using 2 if statements within for loops to make the 2 new varaibles.

Conclusion

The analysis found that grape quality ratings tend to decrease as the Weather Impact Index increases. This suggests that higher environmental stress negatively impacts grape quality. Additionally, regions like Rioja produced larger median grape sizes compared to Barossa Valley, suggesting regional differences in grape growth. Seasonal patterns were also observed, as grapes harvested later in the season, particularly in September, generally had a lower Weather Impact Index, indicating that they were exposed to more favorable growth conditions compared to earlier harvests. These findings suggest that both regional characteristics and seasonal environmental factors play crucial roles in determining grape quality.
